questions.question: Starches found in bread, cereals and pasta are made up of long chains of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**glucose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Carbohydrates: 

 
 
• **Carbohydrates, or carbs, are sugar molecules.**
 
• Along with proteins and fats, **carbohydrates **are one of the three main nutrients found in foods and drinks.
 
• **Your body breaks down carbohydrates into glucose.**
 
• Glucose, or blood sugar, is the main source of energy for your body's cells, tissues, and organs.
 
• **Carbohydrates **are found in a wide array of both healthy and unhealthy foods.
 
• Bread, beans, milk, popcorn, potatoes, cookies, spaghetti, soft drinks, corn, and cherry pie.
 
• The most common and abundant forms are sugars, fibres, and starches.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• **Glycogen, starch and cellulose are polymers of Glucose.**
 
• **Polymers **are materials made of long, **repeating chains of molecules.**
 
• **Glycogen **serves as a form of energy storage in humans, animals, fungi, and bacteria.
 
• **Starch **is a polymer made by plants to store energy.
 
• **Cellulose **is the main substance that makes up the cell walls and fibers of plants.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a chemical compound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Air**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A chemical compound is composed of two or more separate elements.
 
• Chemical compounds are made up of two or more elements that are chemically bound together in a fixed number or ratio.
 
• The constituents of a **compound **can only be separated by either chemical or electrochemical methods (like extraction) while **mixtures **can be separated into their constituents via physical separation methods such as filtration. Thus, the separation of mixtures is relatively easier than the separation of chemical compounds.
 
• Two atoms of the same element bonded in a molecule do not form a chemical compound, it has to be a different element.
 
• Air is a mixture and not a compound because of the following reasons: Air can be separated into its constituents such as oxygen, nitrogen, etc. by fractional distillation of liquid air.
 
• Air shows the properties of all the gases present in it.
 
 
• **Water - H₂O**
 
• **Baking soda - NaHCO₃**
 
• **Common Salt - NaCl**
 
 
 
• **Hence, the air is not a chemical compound, it is a mixture.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A mixture is made up of two or more different substances in which the identities of substances are retained.
 
• A mixture is a compound made up of two or more chemical components that are not chemically linked.
 
• The mixture can be homogenous, or heterogeneous.
 
• An element is chemically the simplest substance and hence cannot be broken down using chemical reactions.

questions.question: The members of a family of an element that all have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons are called ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**isotopes**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Isotopes**

 
• If two atoms have different numbers of protons, they are different elements. However,** if two atoms have the same number of protons, but different numbers of neutrons we refer to them as isotopes**.
 
• **Two terms we use to identify nuclides (isotopes) are atomic number and mass number. Two atoms with the same atomic number, but different mass numbers (same number of protons, different number of neutrons), are called isotopes, or isotopic nuclides.**
 
• Having different numbers of neutrons changes the mass of these atoms, so isotopes have slight variations in their physical and chemical behavior. Some elements have many different isotopes, some only have a few, and some have no stable isotopes at all.
 
• All atoms of the same element have the same number of protons, but some may have different numbers of neutrons. For example, all carbon atoms have six protons, and most have six neutrons as well. But some carbon atoms have seven or eight neutrons instead of the usual six. Atoms of the same element that differ in their numbers of neutrons are called isotopes. Many isotopes occur naturally. Usually, one or two isotopes of an element are the most stable and common. Different isotopes of an element generally have the same physical and chemical properties. That's because they have the same numbers of protons and electrons.
 
• Hydrogen is an example of an element that has isotopes. Most hydrogen atoms have just one proton and one electron and lack a neutron. These atoms are just called hydrogen. Some hydrogen atoms have one neutron as well. These atoms are the isotope named deuterium. Other hydrogen atoms have two neutrons. These atoms are the isotope named tritium.

questions.question: Water which is purified and fit for drinking is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**potable water.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Water which is purified and fit for drinking is known as **Potable water.**
 
• Potable water is water that has been either treated, cleaned or filtered and meets established drinking water standards or is assumed to be reasonably free of harmful bacteria and contaminants, and considered safe to drink or use in cooking and baking.
 
• **Examples of potable water** would be that from treated municipal water systems, water that has been UV filtered, water distilled, or purified by reverse osmosis.
 
• The total count of bacteria in potable water should not exceed **10 per cc.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Soft water is surface water that contains low concentrations of ions and in particular, is low in ions of calcium and magnesium.
 
• Hard water is surface water that contains more than 50 mg/l of calcium carbonate.
 
• Hard water has high mineral content.
 
• This is formed as water percolates into layers of calcium, chalk, or gypsum that are mainly composed of carbonates of calcium and magnesium, bicarbonates, and sulfates.

questions.question: Due to which of the following reactions are household bleaching agents using phosphorous, sulphur and chlorine formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the **__Disproportionation reaction.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Disproportionation reactions are the reason behind household bleaching agents using phosphorous, sulfur, and chlorine formed.**
 
• **Disproportionation reaction**:
 
 
• A disproportionation reaction is a specific type of redox reaction in which a species is simultaneously reduced and oxidized to form two different products.
 
• Electronic configuration of Cl is 1s²,2s²,2p⁶,3s²,3p⁵
 
• It can exhibit a maximum oxidation state of +7.
 
• In the given question, all three species can exhibit a Disproportionation reaction which simultaneously oxidizes as well as reduce.
 
• ClO - cannot undergo oxidation as +7 is the maximum oxidation state exhibited by Chlorine.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A displacement reaction:**

 
 
• It is a type of reaction in which part of one reactant is replaced by another reactant.
 
• There are two types of displacement reactions.
 
 
• **Single displacement reactions**: These are those reactions in which one reactant replaces part of the other. Eg: Fe + CuSO4 → FeSO4 + Cu.
 
• **Double displacement reactions:** These are those reactions in which the cations and anions in the reactants switch partners to form products. Eg: AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO3.
 
 
 
• A displacement reaction is also known as a** replacement reaction or a metathesis reaction.**
 
 
 
• **Combination reaction:**
 
 
• A combination reaction also termed a synthesis reaction is about two or more reactants or substances combining with each other to form a new product.
 
• Rust, which is a result of a combination reaction of oxygen and iron could serve as one of the examples of a combination reaction.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition reaction:**
 
 
• Those reactions in which a compound splits up into two or simpler substances are known as decomposition reactions.
 
• A decomposition reaction is the opposite of a combination reaction.
 
 
• **Thermal decomposition:**
 
 
• When a decomposition reaction is carried out by heating, it is called thermal decomposition. The decomposition reaction of calcium carbonate into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide is an example of thermal decomposition. Example: 2FeSO4 - Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3.

questions.question: How many oxygen atoms are there in a molecule of ozone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Three.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are **three** oxygen atoms in a molecule of ozone.
 
• **Ozone:**
 
 
• A layer of ozone is present in the stratosphere of Earth and prevents the UV rays from reaching the Earth's surface.
 
• It is an allotrope of Oxygen.
 
• **Ozone, or tri-oxygen, is an inorganic molecule with the chemical formula O₃.**
 
• It is a pale blue gas with a distinctively pungent smell.
 
• Ozone is an excellent oxidizing agent as it breaks down into oxygen gas and nascent oxygen. {O₃ - 0₂ +[0]}
 
• It is an allotrope of oxygen that is much less stable than the diatomic allotrope O₂, breaking down in the lower atmosphere to O₂ or di-oxygen.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The upper stratosphere consists of a considerable amount of **ozone (**O3**)**, which protects us from the harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation coming from the sun.
 
• These radiations cause skin cancer (melanoma) in humans. Therefore, it is important to maintain the ozone shield.
 
• Ozone in the stratosphere is a product of UV radiations acting on dioxygen (O₂) molecules. The UV radiations split apart molecular oxygen into free oxygen (O) atoms.
 
• These oxygen atoms combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is CORRECT in relation to chemical bases?

options.text: Bases are sticky to touch, sour to taste and corrosive.
Bases are soapy to touch, bitter to taste and corrosive.
Bases are soapy to touch, sour to taste and corrosive.
Bases are sticky to touch, bitter to taste and corrosive.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bases are soapy to touch, bitter to taste and corrosive.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Properties of Bases

 
 
• Some properties, like a bitter taste, are owned by all bases.

 
 
• The bases** feel slippery, too.**
 
• Furthermore, when immersed in water, bases conduct electricity because they consist of charged particles in the solution.
 
 
 
• They are found to have a **soapy texture** when touched.
 
• These substances release hydroxide ions (OH– ions) when dissolved in water.
 
• In their aqueous solutions, bases act as good conductors of electricity.
 
• The pH values corresponding to bases are always greater than 7.
 
• Bases are bitter-tasting substances that have the ability to turn red litmus paper blue.__
 
• Examples: Sodium hydroxide [NaOH], milk of magnesia [Mg(OH)2], calcium hydroxide [Ca(OH)2].
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• Properties of Acids

 
 
• Acids are corrosive in nature.
 
• They are good conductors of electricity.
 
• Their pH values are always less than 7.
 
• When reacted with metals, these substances produce hydrogen gas.
 
• Acids are sour-tasting substances.
 
• Examples: Sulfuric acid, Hydrochloric acid, Acetic acid.

questions.question:
Which of the following pair of compound name - formula is correct?

I. Hydrogen chloride - H₂Cl

II. Hydrogen sulphide - HS₂
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither I nor II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Hydrogen chloride:**

 
 
• ​Having the chemical formula** HCl**, the substance hydrogen chloride is a **hydrogen halide.**
 
• HCl is a** colourless gas** with a **strong smell.**
 
• The aqueous solution of hydrogen chloride is** hydrochloric acid.**
 
• HCl is **water soluble.**
 
• It turns into a **colourless liquid at 189 K** and a **white solid at 159 K **when it freezes.
 
• **Chlorine, aqua regia, and other chlorides** are made using HCl.
 
• In order to **dissolve noble gases,** it serves as a solvent.
 
• In labs, it serves as a **reagent.**
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen sulphide:**
 
 
• Hydrogen sulphide has an offensively **awful smell** that is comparable to that of **rotting eggs.**
 
• **Chalcogen hydride ga**s having the chemical formula **H₂S** is known as** hydrogen sulfide.**
 
• It is a **dangerous, combustible, and highly corrosive **gas.
 
• For the purpose of analytical chemistry, it is used to** identify cations**.
 
• The **precursor to elemental sulfur** is hydrogen sulfide.
 
• Hydrogen sulfide is used to synthesize a number of **organosulfur compounds**, including **methanethiol, ethanethiol, and thioglycolic acid**.
 
• **Metallic sulphides,** many of which are utilized in the paint industry, are prepared **using hydrogen sulfide.**
 
• The **Girdler sulfide technique** is used to extract **deuterium oxide or heavy water** from regular water.​

questions.question: Which of the following acids is responsible for muscle fatigue in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Lactic Acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lactic acid** is a byproduct of anaerobic metabolism, in which the body produces energy without using oxygen.
 
• It forms when the body breaks down carbohydrates to use for energy when oxygen levels are low.
 
• It is responsible for** muscle fatigue** and **tissue damage**.
 
• But lactic acid is an important **fuel source** for muscles during exercise, including those in the heart.
 
• **Effects of Lactic Acids in body: **
 
 
• More than normal lactic acid levels can lead to a condition called **lactic acidosis **which can lead to muscle weakness, rapid breathing, vomiting, sweating, coma.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Molecular formula of Lactic Acid is** CH3CH(OH)COOH**.
 
• [IMAGE: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/7_Milchs%C3%A4ure.svg/800px-7_Milchs%C3%A4ure.svg.png] 
 
• Sources- sour milk products such as kumis, laban, yogurt, kefir, and some cottage cheeses.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary component of quartz?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Silica**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Quartz**__

 __
 
• **It is a widely distributed mineral of many varieties that consists primarily of silica, or silicon dioxide (SiO₂). Hence, Option 2 is correct.**
 
• Minor impurities such as lithium, sodium, potassium, and titanium may be present.
 
• Quartz has attracted attention from the earliest times; water-clear crystals were known to the ancient Greeks as krystallos—hence the name crystal, or more commonly rock crystal, applied to this variety.
 
• **The name quartz is an old German word of uncertain origin first used by Georgius Agricola in 1530.**
 
• **Quartz is our most common mineral. Quartz is made of the two most abundant chemical elements on Earth: oxygen and silicon**.
 
• Atoms of oxygen and silicon join together as tetrahedrons (three-sided pyramids). This stack together to build crystals. Billions of tetrahedrons are needed to build even a small crystal.
 
• Quartz is an almost pure chemical compound with constant physical properties.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aluminium **__

 __
 
• **It is a chemical element with the symbol Al and atomic number 13. **
 
• Aluminium has a density lower than those of other common metals, at approximately one-third that of steel.
 
• It has a great affinity towards oxygen and forms a protective layer of oxide on the surface when exposed to air. 
 
 
 
• **Zinc**__
 __
 
• It is **a trace mineral**, meaning that the body only needs small amounts, and yet it is necessary for almost 100 enzymes to carry out vital chemical reactions.
 
• **It is a major player in the creation of DNA, growth of cells, building proteins, healing of damaged tissue, and supporting a healthy immune system.**
 
 
 
• **Iron**__
 
 
• It is **a mineral that is naturally present in many foods, added to some food products, and available as a dietary supplement**.
 
• Iron is an essential component of haemoglobin, an erythrocyte (red blood cell) protein that transfers oxygen from the lungs to the tissues.
